findings: The legend's lower-left corner sits close to a warm-shaded cluster in the far northwest; near enough that partial overlap can't be ruled out from the image, though it doesn't clearly cover a substantial area.

Serving and non-serving markers overlap into dense clusters in several places, so I could not visually confirm the claim that non-serving crosses (897) look sparser than serving dots (354); crosses appear concentrated in fewer, denser blobs while dots are more individually spread, which is a different pattern than 'sparser', not clearly the same or contradictory.

All 14 numbers 1-14 are present exactly once. Service-radius circles are consistently a few percent of frame width, consistent with 1000 m on a 48 km frame; no gross unit error visible. Sites sit in or beside tan (unserved) areas, including the isolated site 13 near a matching isolated tan patch. No two markers appear closer than the minimum separation. Legend distinguishes recommended sites from existing facilities.
